# Diagnostics: Constant high-pitched squeaking noises

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Inspect rear spring bushings, front sway bar bushings, LCA ball joints, body metal cracks, fender folds, and heat shields. [t1877]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Inspect the rear spring bushings for wear.
2. Check the front sway bar bushings if not already replaced.
3. Examine the LCA ball joints by jacking up the truck on the cross member to let the suspension hang freely, then shake the tires in/out and lift them to check joint movement.
4. Look at the body metal around the headlights for cracks causing metal-on-metal squeaks.
5. Inspect where the front fender sheet metal folds under the hood and bolts to the body; look for cracked sheet metal that moves with suspension travel.
6. Locate two heat shields bolted to the underside of the driver-side body above the catalytic converter, fastened by threaded studs and 10mm nuts.
7. Attempt to tighten or loosen the 10mm nuts on the upper shield; if it still flexes and squeaks, try bending the shield for clearance (though this may not solve a high-pitched rub).
8. [Partial] Apply lithium grease between the heat shield and body as an alternative fix before resorting to other methods.
9. If all else fails or access is tight, wedge a length of high-temp fuel line between the heat shield and the body.

_Procedure reported by [t1877]._
